- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecasted drop magnitude.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; cap forecast decline to 5–8% below peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model frequently underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecasted lows.
- Model tends to overestimate short-term mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 day horizon) when sentiment is volatile; smooth out sharp reversals.
- When sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts continuation; adjust downward only if sentiment > 0.10.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price lows in early 20–30 days; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to early forecasted lows.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts continuation; adjust upward only if sentiment < -0.20.
